content: In Nafsat I, per Melvin-Koushki, the first fault is that ecstatic Sufis say things that seem to be unbelief; lazy good-for-nothings seize on these, reduce them to ‘Everything is God’ and become heretics, citing the poetry of Aḥmad-i Jām, Rūmī, ʿIrāqī and others, which leads rulers to think all Sufis are of their type and to trust anti-Sufi scholars.
